title: A tall blackbearded figure, bent on a stick, stumping round the corner of Elvery’s Elephant house, showed them a curved hand open on his spine.
html_source:
They are referring to Reuben J. Dodd, an actual citizen of Dublin who, inter alia, was a money lender. There are further references to him throughout Ulysses. All the characters in the book, including Bloom, appear to assume Dodd is Jewish, although in life he was not. Joyce himself almost certainly knew this, since for a time he was acquainted with Reuben J. Dodd’s son when they both attended the same Catholic school.

Elvery’s Elephant house, Ireland’s oldest sports store selling sporting goods and waterproof wear, was located at 46 & 47 Lower Sackville Street, corner of Abbey Street. The shop had a distinctive figure of an elephant above the front door – hence its name.
